unsat.note: BindCraft allows up to 4. A raw count grows with interface size, so keep it soft.

extra.label: Binder RMSD (binder alone vs complex)
extra.note: BindCraft Binder_RMSD: the binder predicted on its own, compared with its shape in the complex. BindCraft rejects designs above 3.5 Å.
rescue: Re-predict the binder alone with a second model; discard if it still differs from the complex shape

extra.label: Atoms within 3 Å of the other subunit
extra.note: The design is placed on the reference assembly. A binder that overlaps another subunit could not bind the assembled protein. Overlap fails a design; contact at the subunit interface is a warning.
rescue: Add the other subunit as fixed context, or move the binder to a face that stays exposed in the assembly

nl.text: At most 9 atoms within 3 Å of the other subunit

extra.label: Contacted residues at the subunit interface
extra.note: Contacted residues that another subunit buries in the assembly. A surface that is part of the subunit interface may not exist on the assembled protein.
rescue: Keep as a hedge, or discard if the goal is a binder of the intact assembly

extra.label: Atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein
extra.note: BindCraft only saw the construct. The rest of the same chain (the removed regions) is placed from the reference structure; a binder that overlaps it could not bind the full-length protein.
rescue: Include the neighbouring domain in the target, or move the binder away from that face

nl.text: At most 9 atoms within 3 Å of the rest of the protein

extra.label: Contacts next to a cut end
extra.note: Contacted residues within a few residues of a cut end of the construct, or of a deleted loop. A surface next to a cut can be exposed only because the rest of the protein is missing.
rescue: Extend the target by 10 to 15 residues and re-run, or discard

extra.label: Contacted residues buried in the full protein
extra.note: Contacted residues that the removed regions would bury (more than the area set in the profile). These contacts may not exist on the full-length protein.
rescue: Include the covering region in the target and re-run

examples.label: On the hotspots, fits the assembly
examples.q: On the hotspots, clear of the other subunit, at most 1 buried unsatisfied polar

examples.label: Clear of the rest of the protein
examples.q: Away from the rest of the protein and the cut ends, no sticky hydrophobic patch

cards.title: Detected: RFdiffusion 4 · {n_runs} runs
cards.html: {n_designs} designs that pass your import cutoffs, plus {n_rejected} that miss them (kept for near-miss rescue). Acceptance is your cutoffs, applied per required target chain; RFD4's own motif_scaffold.pass is shown beside them. Families appear only when beam-search siblings share a backbone.

cards.title: Target frame
cards.html: Every target chain the design engages is the target. Per-chain AF3 scores (ipTM, min iPAE) gate acceptance: a design must clear the bar on each required chain. Partner chains are drawn as structures, not CA traces.

cards.title: Read, recomputed, missing
cards.html:
Read: AF3 oracle scores (pLDDT, ipTM, iPAE, ranking, clash, motif and backbone RMSD when present), per-partner pairwise scores, contig motif segments and C_HOT hotspots.
Recomputed: interface on each target chain, H-bonds, buried area, context against avoid-marked partners, the design/re-score pair (generated vs AF3 refold).
Not available: Rosetta block, MPNN scores, PAE matrix / ipSAE, per-validation-model columns. Those meters switch off.

text.badge.title.board: Designs and scores come from RFdiffusion 4 with AlphaFold 3. The analysed pose is the AF3 refold; the dashed ghost is the generated design. Cutoffs are yours. Every score is a screen, not a verdict.
text.badge.title.inspector: Binder models are RFD4 AF3 complexes. Contacts, hydrogen bonds, buried polars and context checks are recomputed. Per-chain AF3 scores gate acceptance on every required partner.
text.badge.title.map: Designs and scores come from RFdiffusion 4. Where orthologs or paralogs were given, they are UniProt sequences aligned to the target construct.
text.badge.title.query: Designs and scores come from RFdiffusion 4, accepted and rejected under your import cutoffs. Rules are typed and editable.
